title: Extension by zero and lower shriek of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, with module objects
$\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ over $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ ([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients],
[sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), and write $j^{\Ab}_!\dashv j^*_{\Ab}$
for the extension by zero and the pullback of abelian sheaves along an open immersion
$j\colon U\to X$ ([sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek],
[def-sfb-finite-upper-star] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$).

- *Projection formula.* For $L\in\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and
  $M\in\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ the canonical map
  $j^{\Ab}_!(j^*_{\Ab}L\otimes M)\to L\otimes j^{\Ab}_!M$ is an isomorphism
  (tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]).
- *Linear extension by zero.* By the projection formula, $j^{\Ab}_!$ linearizes
  ([sk-def-sfb-transport]) to a functor
  $j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\colon\Mod_{j^*\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, sending $M$ to
  $j^{\Ab}_!M$ with the action
  $\Lambda_X\otimes j^{\Ab}_!M\cong j^{\Ab}_!(j^*\Lambda_X\otimes M)\to j^{\Ab}_!M$;
  it is left adjoint to $\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$.
- *Extension by zero.* The extension by zero of module objects is
  $$
  j_!:=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\colon
  \Mod_{\Lambda_U}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}
  $$
  ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). The underlying
  sheaf of $j_!M$ is $j^{\Ab}_!M$; $j_!$ is exact, and $j_!\dashv j^*$ with $j^*$ the
  pullback of module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]).
- *Lower shriek.* For a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$
  of a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$, in particular $f=g\circ i$ with $i$ an open immersion and $g$
  proper ([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]),
  $$
  f^c_!:=g_*\circ i_!\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y},
  $$
  and for $f$ admitting a compactification, $f_!:=f^c_!$ for a chosen compactification
  $c$ of $f$. The underlying sheaf of $f_!M$ is the lower shriek of abelian sheaves
  of $M$ for the same compactification, and $f_!$ is left exact.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-open-projection-formula] for the given open immersion $j$ and the abelian sheaves $L,M$. Its canonical map is defined as the adjoint of $j^*_{\Ab}L\otimes M\to j^*_{\Ab}(L\otimes j^{\Ab}_!M)$ using the unit of $j^{\Ab}_!\dashv j^*_{\Ab}$, exactly the projection map of the statement, and the cited lemma asserts that it is an isomorphism. No restriction on $L$ or $M$ is imposed.

Take the linear extension by zero of [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek] for the same $\Lambda$ and $j$. Its source is $\Mod_{j^*\Lambda_X}$ and its target is $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. On an action $\gamma_M:j^*\Lambda_X\otimes M\to M$ it has action $\Lambda_X\otimes j^{\Ab}_!M\cong j^{\Ab}_!(j^*\Lambda_X\otimes M)\xrightarrow{j^{\Ab}_!\gamma_M}j^{\Ab}_!M$, using the inverse of the projection isomorphism from step 1. This is precisely the linearization operation of [sk-def-sfb-transport], parts 3 and 4. On a module morphism it applies $j^{\Ab}_!$. The cited linear-extension node also gives the lifted adjunction $j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$ and exactness.

For $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_U}$ restrict its action along $\alpha_j:j^*\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ and then apply step 2. Thus $j_!=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ is the functor of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Restriction changes the action by precomposing with $\alpha_j\otimes1$ and leaves underlying objects and morphisms unchanged ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], part 1). Consequently the underlying sheaf is $j^{\Ab}_!M$. Exactness is explicitly asserted for this composite in [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], for an arbitrary commutative condensed ring and an arbitrary open immersion.

The coefficient morphism $\alpha_j$ is an isomorphism of ring objects by the last sentence of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]; this statement applies to every condensed ring, not only to a selected list of coefficients. Apply [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], parts 3 and 5, in $\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$: equalizers of abelian sheaves are computed objectwise (the equalizer of the two sheaf-condition bijections is again a bijection), and coequalizers are the sheafifications of the objectwise cokernels of the difference of the maps (the sheafification adjunction gives the required universal property); its tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and preserves colimits in each variable by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The ring $j^*\Lambda_X$ is commutative, and $\alpha_j$ is invertible. These give $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}$ and $\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j^{-1}}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}$. This is the scalar adjunction and its identification $\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}$ appearing explicitly in [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]. For $M\in\Mod_{\Lambda_U}$ and $N\in\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ the natural Hom bijections are
$$
\Hom(j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}M,N)
\cong\Hom(\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}M,\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})N)
\cong\Hom(M,\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_j}\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})N)
\cong\Hom(M,\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})N).
$$
The first bijection is the linear adjunction of step 2, and the second and third are precisely the scalar adjunction and identification in the cited adjunction node. The last argument is $j^*N$ by [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. This proves $j_!\dashv j^*$ with the required direction of restriction of scalars.

Given the specified compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, define $f^c_!$ to be $g_*\circ i_!$ as in [def-sfb-module-compactification-lower-shriek]. The functor $i_!$ lands in $\Mod_{\Lambda_{\bar X}}$ and $g_*$ starts in that same category, so this is a functor $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$. For a chosen compactification define $f_!$ to be this functor, as in [def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. These are definitions for the specified choice; no comparison between different compactifications is used.

By [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] the underlying sheaf of $i_!M$ is $i^{\Ab}_!M$, and by [def-sfb-module-lower-star] the underlying sheaf of $g_*N$ is $g^{\Ab}_*N$. Hence the underlying sheaf functor of the composite is $g^{\Ab}_*i^{\Ab}_!$, the abelian lower shriek for this same compactification ([sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]). The two module functors are additive, $i_!$ is exact, and $g_*$ is left exact by the two cited module nodes. In particular each preserves the zero object and kernels. For a module map $a$, $g_*i_!(\ker a)\cong g_*(\ker(i_!a))\cong\ker(g_*i_!a)$; thus their additive composite is left exact, as asserted.
